name: Keoladeo National Park
description: Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan, India, is a 29 square kilometre patch of wetlands, woodland and grassland that began as a duck-shooting reserve for the Maharajas in 1899. Each winter, thousands of waterbirds arrive from as far as Siberia, China and Afghanistan, and hundreds of species have been recorded. Visitors often explore its flat paths by bicycle or rickshaw.
